raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Expose the actual draft-token verification budget when adaptive verification is enabled. The existing draft counter counts proposals, which may be longer than the prefix sent to the target verifier.

This PR adds:

- `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_draft_tokens_total` and the verified count in server logs.
- `vllm:spec_decode_num_verified_draft_tokens_per_pos_total{position="..."}`, with zero-based positions. A verified prefix of length 3 increments positions 0, 1, and 2; the sum across positions equals the scalar verified count.
- `num_verified_draft_tokens` in the per-request speculative decoding metrics (`--per-request-spec-decode-metrics`), plus `per_step_verified` at the `detailed` level (from @tomasruizt, with the field renamed to match `num_accepted_draft_tokens`).
- Documentation and unit tests for verified-token accounting.

The verified counters and per-request fields are exposed only with adaptive verification enabled. They exclude bonus tokens and use the same request filtering as proposal accounting, including excluding results for already-finished requests. With async scheduling and structured outputs, grammar-invalid positions can still be physically verified, so verified counts can exceed grammar-adjusted proposal counts. Changing how grammar-invalid drafts are counted is left out of this PR.

MRV2 reports per-request verified lengths through the async output-copy path. The per-position extension reuses the same CPU integers as the scalar counter, adding no further GPU kernel, D2H copy, or synchronization. It adds up to K CPU list increments per observed request, a K-entry stats vector, and K counter updates per observed batch. Overhead has not been benchmarked.

This extends the existing verified-token accounting in this PR. Related #54748 records the scheduler-selected K, including no-draft steps; it measures a different stage from the verifier's actual admitted prefix.

## Validation

CPU-only tests ran from this PR's full Python source on Linux/Python 3.12.3 with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and native artifacts reused from the existing vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev183+g7e3d55956 environment. No GPU serving or model evaluation was run for the per-position or per-request changes.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py -v
```

```text
============================== 21 passed in 2.41s ==============================
```

Using a local Hugging Face cache containing OPT-125M config/tokenizer files:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  HF_HUB_CACHE=/opt/pr58340_per_position_20261022/hf-cache OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
    -k "spec_decoding_stats or adaptive_verification_stats_count_actual_budget" -v
```

```text
====================== 11 passed, 196 deselected in 4.34s ======================
```

Coverage includes different prefix distributions with the same verified total, zero/missing verified counts, AV-disabled metric gating, stats serialization, grammar-invalid positions (verified count only), finished-request filtering, and the per-request fields with and without adaptive verification. The new position assertions fail on the preceding commit because the per-position verified field is absent.

For the per-request commits, using the same environment and local OPT-125M cache:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
    -k "adaptive_verification or per_request_spec" --confcutdir=tests/v1 -v
```

```text
====================== 8 passed, 200 deselected in 35.46s ======================
```

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_request_acceptance.py \
    tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py --confcutdir=tests/v1 -q
```

```text
32 passed in 14.63s
```

`tests/test_outputs.py -k spec_decode` also passed, and an ad-hoc script confirmed the new fields survive the `EngineCoreOutputs` msgpack round trip and reach `SpeculativeDecodingMetrics`.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  docs/features/speculative_decoding/acceptance_metrics.md
```

All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, Markdown lint, test tethering, and mypy for Python 3.10. The commit hooks also passed.

nodes.body:
This fills a real gap — with adaptive verification `num_draft_tokens` counts proposals and
nothing counted what the target actually verified. Two notes, one on composition and one on
the shape.

**This and `spec_decode_scheduled_k` are complements, not overlaps.** I have #54748 open
adding the K the schedule *resolved*, including the K=0 steps that currently increment no
counter at all. That is the scheduler's decision; yours is what survived the verifier's
trim. With both, `scheduled_k → draft_tokens → verified → accepted` is a closed chain; with
either alone there is a step where tokens vanish with no accounting line. They touch
different hunks of `update_from_output`, so they compose — I mention it only so the overlap
in files does not read as duplicated work.

**On the shape.** Your doc note is right that the mean is derivable: `observe_draft` is
called per request (`make_spec_decoding_stats` takes a `request_id`,
`scheduler.py:2885-2899`), so `num_drafts` counts drafting requests and
`verified / num_drafts` is mean admitted depth. My concern is not that the denominator is
missing — it is that a mean is the wrong summary for how this budget is actually spent.

`_assign_draft_token_budget` scores every `(request, step)` slot by survival probability and
admits a **global top-k** across the batch, then writes the per-request result back into
`capacities` — its docstring says so directly: `capacities` "enters holding each request's
scheduled draft count ... and leaves holding the admitted count"
(`adaptive_verification.py:61-63`). A global top-k concentrates by construction: confident
requests keep their full depth and unconfident ones are zeroed. So with 40 drafting
requests and 40 verified positions, mean admitted depth is 1.0 whether every request kept
exactly one, or four kept ten and thirty-six kept none. Those are opposite operating
conditions — a uniform shave versus a subset losing speculation entirely — and the mean
reports them identically. `num_verified_draft_tokens` is the sum of `capacities`, so the
distribution is discarded one step before it is exported.

The shape that answers it without unbounded labels already exists in the file you are
editing: `SpecDecodingStats` carries `num_accepted_tokens_per_pos` and
`num_draft_tokens_per_pos` (`spec_decode/metrics.py:30-31`), exported through the
per-position counter machinery at `:247-281`. A `num_verified_draft_tokens_per_pos` completes
that triple — proposed, verified, accepted, all keyed on draft index — at a vector length of
`num_spec_tokens`, cardinality this file already spends twice. "Position 5 is proposed but
never verified" then reads straight off it, and the concentrated case separates from the
uniform one because the tail buckets differ.

The honest cost: `capacities` is an `int32` device tensor (`:162-164`) that currently never
leaves the GPU — it is consumed in place by the `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc` cumsums
(`:432-442`). Filling a per-position vector needs it on the host, so this adds a
synchronisation to a per-step path. A device-side `bincount` into `num_spec_tokens + 1`
buckets keeps the transfer to a fixed small vector rather than `num_reqs`, and it may fold
into a sync already happening nearby, but I cannot settle that from outside and it is
reasonable to land the scalar first and treat the vector as a follow-up.

Disclosure: #54748 is mine and the closed chain above is better for it existing. Nothing
here depends on that PR landing and I am not asking you to reference it; the distribution
point stands on its own.

We can also get the `num_verified_toks` in the server logs, it looks like this:
```log
... SpecDecoding metrics: ... Accepted: 1150 tokens, Drafted: 3760 tokens, Verified: 3754 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate:  ...
```
here is the code: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/fef2689a5aff73733acd4b88066109272aced9dd

PS: I'm seeing some suspicious lines where `num_verified > num_drafted` like below (full [server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33149765/server.log))
```log
Drafted: 7024 tokens, Verified: 7050 tokens
```
It doesn't seems to be related to this PR, but rather to the counting differing compared to `num_drafted`: 
1. When a request is finished, their `num_drafted` are not counted, even though the verification work already happened (async-scheduling?).
2. `num_invalid_tokens` is subtracted from `num_drafted` e.g. in structured output (introduced https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29821)

I will dive deeper into this to make sure the invariant `num_drafted` >= `num_verified` is respected by the metrics.

To respect the invariant`num_drafted >= num_verified` we can track the verified tokens _per request_ rather than _per batch_. Meaning we `observe()` verified and drafted tokens at the same time once per request. This way, requests that are skipped don't break the invariant (e.g. when the req was completed last step in async-scheduling). Code: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/6dc1cb82008a430593f8edbebd64dc80a5c63529

The new server logs show the invariant is respected: [server-after.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33167729/server-after.log)

Thanks @tomasruizt for running the experiments and for your suggestions!
Both the logging and per-request accounting changes make sense to me. I've rebased onto main and cherry-picked your three commits, preserving your authorship and sign-offs.
I also added a regression test and documented why the verified count can exceed the grammar-adjusted draft count with async scheduling and structured outputs.

cc @benchislett PTAL

As discussed with @benchislett and @yzong-rh, we should support not only the prometheus metric but also the per-request acceptance metrics (they are documented here: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/speculative_decoding/acceptance_metrics/)

This should be relatively straightforward, I have a suggestion here: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/a8d6af6149

We also discussed whether to subtract grammar-invalid tokens: probably the solution is to not subtract them from drafted-tokens in the first place, and to sharpen the distinction between drafted-tokens and verified-tokens. The downstream effects of doing this have to be validated. As well as the interaction with async-scheduling + structured output and sync-scheduling.

Thanks @tomasruizt @benchislett @yzong-rh for discussing this.

- Per-request metrics: I've added @tomasruizt's per-request commit (a8d6af6), with the field renamed to `num_verified_draft_tokens` to match `num_accepted_draft_tokens` and the Prometheus counter. With adaptive verification, `metrics.speculative_decoding` now includes `num_verified_draft_tokens`, plus `per_step_verified` at the `detailed` level.
- Grammar-invalid drafts: I agree the subtraction from the drafted count should be removed, but I'd like to leave it out of this PR for now. I've also removed the drafted-count assertion from the grammar-invalid test case, so it now only checks the verified count.

@benchislett does this address the blocking concern?

issue_comments.body:
This fills a real gap — with adaptive verification `num_draft_tokens` counts proposals and
nothing counted what the target actually verified. Two notes, one on composition and one on
the shape.

**This and `spec_decode_scheduled_k` are complements, not overlaps.** I have #54748 open
adding the K the schedule *resolved*, including the K=0 steps that currently increment no
counter at all. That is the scheduler's decision; yours is what survived the verifier's
trim. With both, `scheduled_k → draft_tokens → verified → accepted` is a closed chain; with
either alone there is a step where tokens vanish with no accounting line. They touch
different hunks of `update_from_output`, so they compose — I mention it only so the overlap
in files does not read as duplicated work.

**On the shape.** Your doc note is right that the mean is derivable: `observe_draft` is
called per request (`make_spec_decoding_stats` takes a `request_id`,
`scheduler.py:2885-2899`), so `num_drafts` counts drafting requests and
`verified / num_drafts` is mean admitted depth. My concern is not that the denominator is
missing — it is that a mean is the wrong summary for how this budget is actually spent.

`_assign_draft_token_budget` scores every `(request, step)` slot by survival probability and
admits a **global top-k** across the batch, then writes the per-request result back into
`capacities` — its docstring says so directly: `capacities` "enters holding each request's
scheduled draft count ... and leaves holding the admitted count"
(`adaptive_verification.py:61-63`). A global top-k concentrates by construction: confident
requests keep their full depth and unconfident ones are zeroed. So with 40 drafting
requests and 40 verified positions, mean admitted depth is 1.0 whether every request kept
exactly one, or four kept ten and thirty-six kept none. Those are opposite operating
conditions — a uniform shave versus a subset losing speculation entirely — and the mean
reports them identically. `num_verified_draft_tokens` is the sum of `capacities`, so the
distribution is discarded one step before it is exported.

The shape that answers it without unbounded labels already exists in the file you are
editing: `SpecDecodingStats` carries `num_accepted_tokens_per_pos` and
`num_draft_tokens_per_pos` (`spec_decode/metrics.py:30-31`), exported through the
per-position counter machinery at `:247-281`. A `num_verified_draft_tokens_per_pos` completes
that triple — proposed, verified, accepted, all keyed on draft index — at a vector length of
`num_spec_tokens`, cardinality this file already spends twice. "Position 5 is proposed but
never verified" then reads straight off it, and the concentrated case separates from the
uniform one because the tail buckets differ.

The honest cost: `capacities` is an `int32` device tensor (`:162-164`) that currently never
leaves the GPU — it is consumed in place by the `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc` cumsums
(`:432-442`). Filling a per-position vector needs it on the host, so this adds a
synchronisation to a per-step path. A device-side `bincount` into `num_spec_tokens + 1`
buckets keeps the transfer to a fixed small vector rather than `num_reqs`, and it may fold
into a sync already happening nearby, but I cannot settle that from outside and it is
reasonable to land the scalar first and treat the vector as a follow-up.

Disclosure: #54748 is mine and the closed chain above is better for it existing. Nothing
here depends on that PR landing and I am not asking you to reference it; the distribution
point stands on its own.

We can also get the `num_verified_toks` in the server logs, it looks like this:
```log
... SpecDecoding metrics: ... Accepted: 1150 tokens, Drafted: 3760 tokens, Verified: 3754 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate:  ...
```
here is the code: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/fef2689a5aff73733acd4b88066109272aced9dd

PS: I'm seeing some suspicious lines where `num_verified > num_drafted` like below (full [server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33149765/server.log))
```log
Drafted: 7024 tokens, Verified: 7050 tokens
```
It doesn't seems to be related to this PR, but rather to the counting differing compared to `num_drafted`: 
1. When a request is finished, their `num_drafted` are not counted, even though the verification work already happened (async-scheduling?).
2. `num_invalid_tokens` is subtracted from `num_drafted` e.g. in structured output (introduced https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29821)

I will dive deeper into this to make sure the invariant `num_drafted` >= `num_verified` is respected by the metrics.

To respect the invariant`num_drafted >= num_verified` we can track the verified tokens _per request_ rather than _per batch_. Meaning we `observe()` verified and drafted tokens at the same time once per request. This way, requests that are skipped don't break the invariant (e.g. when the req was completed last step in async-scheduling). Code: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/6dc1cb82008a430593f8edbebd64dc80a5c63529

The new server logs show the invariant is respected: [server-after.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33167729/server-after.log)

Thanks @tomasruizt for running the experiments and for your suggestions!
Both the logging and per-request accounting changes make sense to me. I've rebased onto main and cherry-picked your three commits, preserving your authorship and sign-offs.
I also added a regression test and documented why the verified count can exceed the grammar-adjusted draft count with async scheduling and structured outputs.

cc @benchislett PTAL

As discussed with @benchislett and @yzong-rh, we should support not only the prometheus metric but also the per-request acceptance metrics (they are documented here: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/speculative_decoding/acceptance_metrics/)

This should be relatively straightforward, I have a suggestion here: https://github.com/tomasruizt/vllm/commit/a8d6af6149

We also discussed whether to subtract grammar-invalid tokens: probably the solution is to not subtract them from drafted-tokens in the first place, and to sharpen the distinction between drafted-tokens and verified-tokens. The downstream effects of doing this have to be validated. As well as the interaction with async-scheduling + structured output and sync-scheduling.

Thanks @tomasruizt @benchislett @yzong-rh for discussing this.

- Per-request metrics: I've added @tomasruizt's per-request commit (a8d6af6), with the field renamed to `num_verified_draft_tokens` to match `num_accepted_draft_tokens` and the Prometheus counter. With adaptive verification, `metrics.speculative_decoding` now includes `num_verified_draft_tokens`, plus `per_step_verified` at the `detailed` level.
- Grammar-invalid drafts: I agree the subtraction from the drafted count should be removed, but I'd like to leave it out of this PR for now. I've also removed the drafted-count assertion from the grammar-invalid test case, so it now only checks the verified count.
